Alex Chen: Quick sync — I'm tuning continuous batching heuristics (batch formation, queue policies, token-budget targets) focused on max_batch_size / max_tokens_per_batch per GPU type (A10/T4/L4/A100/H100). Ran a profiling sweep this morning, seeing some surprising regressions with KV-heavy workloads. Need quick opinions on target caps.

Matt O'Neill: Share the profiling numbers?

Alex Chen: Pasted summary below (single-rep runs, 2k context, dynamic KV growth from chat histories):
- A100: peak throughput ~42k tokens/s, p99 ~120ms @ batch_size=64, tokens_per_batch ~8k. Memory headroom still ~18%
- H100: peak throughput ~52k tokens/s, p99 ~95ms @ batch_size=80, tokens_per_batch ~10k. Memory headroom ~12%
- A10: peak throughput ~18k tokens/s, p99 ~240ms @ batch_size=32, tokens_per_batch ~4k. Memory headroom ~24%
- L4: peak throughput ~15k tokens/s, p99 ~200ms @ batch_size=24, tokens_per_batch ~4k. Memory headroom ~30%
- T4: peak throughput ~9k tokens/s, p99 ~380ms @ batch_size=16, tokens_per_batch ~2k. Memory headroom ~28%

Priya Singh: Nice. Two quick things we saw: (1) KV cache growth is the real limiter — if the request mix has long histories, tokens_per_batch needs to be lowered to keep model activations + cache < GPU mem. (2) Kernel selection fallbacks on smaller GPUs (T4/A10) add CPU->GPU overhead when batch shapes vary; that increases p99.

Luca Bianchi: For config recommendations from my experiments last week (mixed short/long chats):
- H100: max_batch_size=96, max_tokens_per_batch=11000, prefer_time_ms=12, prefer_tokens=true
- A100: max_batch_size=72, max_tokens_per_batch=9000, prefer_time_ms=15
- A10: max_batch_size=40, max_tokens_per_batch=4500, prefer_time_ms=30, conservative_kernel=true
- L4: max_batch_size=28, max_tokens_per_batch=4200, prefer_time_ms=35
- T4: max_batch_size=18, max_tokens_per_batch=2200, prefer_time_ms=40, force_single_kernel=true

Priya Singh: Those look reasonable. I'd add an adaptive fallback: if queued KV bytes per-GPU > X (e.g., 6GB), switch to token-budget-first policy and drop prefer_time_ms to 6ms so we flush smaller batches faster. That avoids OOMs during flashbacks.

Alex Chen: Good call. We observed a perf regression on A10 when we increased max_batch_size from 32->48 — latency spiked and throughput fell. Profiling shows increased kernel launch counts and more PCIe stalls.

Matt O'Neill: That's consistent with kernel selection thrashing. On A10 the runtime picks a faster matmul kernel for mid-sized batches but it has worse memory locality with large KV cache, so net is worse. We should constrain batch-size range for A10.

infra-bot: CI-profile job rtx-batch-sweep-1768 finished — attached flamegraphs: https://ci.internal/redwood/profiles/1768 (perm: eng-runtime) :white_check_mark:

Alex Chen: Proposed runtime config snippet to try (rolling canary, per-gpu overrides):

```yaml
continuous_batching:
  global:
    prefer_time_ms: 20
    max_wait_ms: 60
  per_gpu:
    H100:
      max_batch_size: 96
      max_tokens_per_batch: 11000
    A100:
      max_batch_size: 72
      max_tokens_per_batch: 9000
    A10:
      max_batch_size: 32
      max_tokens_per_batch: 4000
      conservative_kernel: true
    L4:
      max_batch_size: 28
      max_tokens_per_batch: 4200
    T4:
      max_batch_size: 16
      max_tokens_per_batch: 2000
      force_single_kernel: true
```

Priya Singh: Suggest we add a runtime probe that measures "queued_kv_bytes" and toggles an override: if queued_kv_bytes > 5GB reduce max_tokens_per_batch by 30% and set prefer_time_ms to 6ms. Also emit metric continuous_batching.evictions when we force-flush due to token cap.

Luca Bianchi: Also don't forget to tune the token_budget_target heuristic: aim for 60-70% mem headroom on GPUs with large KV churn to prevent tail-OOMs. For H100/A100 we can be more aggressive (75-80% target).

Matt O'Neill: Plan: roll this to a small Dedicated pool (mixed L4+A10) first, monitor p95/p99 + queued_kv_bytes + kernel_fallback_count. If p99 regresses >15% revert per-GPU increases.

Alex Chen: I'll push a canary with the YAML above and Priya's KV probe by EOD. Infra-bot — kick off a canary cluster with 4 instances each of A10/L4 and another canary for H100/A100.

infra-bot: Canary creation started: canary-ctch-20260318 (A10/L4) and canary-ctch-20260318-h (A100/H100). Jobs: rtx-batch-canary-1769, rtx-batch-canary-1770.

Priya Singh: One last note — for models using grouped kv (multi-turn chat), we should consider per-request kv-weighting so the batcher can pack more short-history requests together and avoid mixing long-history ones. That reduced tail latency in our internal tests by ~22%.

Alex Chen: Great. Thanks all. I'll post results in this thread once canary metrics are in. :thumbsup:

Matt O'Neill: Thanks — will watch dashboards and set alert on kernel_fallback_count > 5/min.

Luca Bianchi: If anyone wants the raw flamegraphs or perf traces, ping me and I'll share the S3 links.

Alex Chen: pinging @here for awareness in case anyone else sees related regressions.
